gaps.consequence: Callers receive status 'executed' even though no task is dispatched, validated, or completed.
gaps.evidence: executeMission creates a mission, evaluates governance, and returns {status:'executed'}; no adapter, task, evidence, or completion call exists.
gaps.rootCause: The orchestrator is a stub and does not use the mission lifecycle beyond creation.
gaps.remediation: Replace the stub with a task engine that dispatches registered adapters, validates results, records evidence, and completes/fails the mission.
gaps.acceptanceTest: Real shell task completes the mission; failure/timeout/cancel paths never report executed.

gaps.consequence: No typed task contract, status, error taxonomy, acceptance criterion, or result schema exists.
gaps.evidence: Search of schemas finds only Agent metrics; no Task schema.
gaps.rootCause: Task orchestration was never modeled as a first-class domain.
gaps.remediation: Add TaskDefinition, TaskAcceptance, TaskEvidence, TaskResult, TaskStatus and TaskErrorCode schemas.
gaps.acceptanceTest: Malformed adapter results are rejected; task results conform to TaskResultSchema.

gaps.consequence: A caller can assert passing evidence without executing anything; the kernel has no executed-vs-reported distinction.
gaps.evidence: MissionEvidenceSchema has no provenance/executionId/exitCode; completion checks only status/simulated.
gaps.rootCause: Sprint 1 deliberately accepted caller-supplied evidence; no executed-only mode.
gaps.remediation: Add provenance fields and an executed verification mode; require provenance=executed plus executionId for completion.
gaps.acceptanceTest: Executed-mode mission rejects reported and simulated evidence; accepts executed evidence with executionId.

gaps.consequence: No timeouts, retries, cancellation, retry budgets, loop detection, or circuit breaking.
gaps.evidence: The orchestrator has no execution loop, AbortSignal, attempt counter, or failure classifier.
gaps.remediation: Implement bounded retries, per-task deadlines, cancellation, loop detection and per-adapter circuit breakers.
gaps.acceptanceTest: Timeout, cancellation, retry exhaustion, loop detection and open-circuit tests produce explicit terminal outcomes.

gaps.consequence: Agent/adapter output is untrusted and unvalidated; malformed output could be treated as success.
gaps.evidence: No result schema or validation call exists.
gaps.remediation: Validate adapter output with a schema; map malformed output to INVALID_OUTPUT/INVALID_INPUT.
gaps.acceptanceTest: Malformed adapter output fails the task and mission without completion.

gaps.consequence: No correlated mission/task progress events are emitted by the orchestrator.
gaps.evidence: Only transcript/tool output exists; no task event stream.
gaps.remediation: Add an in-process event emitter with typed events and correlation IDs; expose task results through the orchestrator API.
gaps.acceptanceTest: Task lifecycle events are emitted in order for a real execution.

gaps.consequence: Durable audit is opt-in and disabled in this environment; the hash chain is valid but not durable.
gaps.remediation: Keep the existing opt-in sink; document the requirement and test append/restart/tamper paths. Do not silently enable a path.
gaps.acceptanceTest: Existing audit-sink tests pass; final report states durable status truthfully.

gaps.consequence: Human approval is not proven to reach a UI; policy denials are enforced in preflight, but escalation approval is host-specific.
gaps.evidence: Core has deny/escalate verdicts; no approval record is persisted by the orchestrator.
gaps.rootCause: No approval transport in the core orchestrator.
gaps.remediation: Treat escalated tasks as blocked pending an explicit host decision; do not infer approval. Record external dependency.
gaps.acceptanceTest: Escalated governance verdict blocks execution with an explicit approval-required outcome.

gaps.consequence: Async write-through means in-memory rollback cannot prove durable rollback; no nested savepoints.
gaps.rootCause: Postgres adapter batches async writes and reports at flush.
gaps.remediation: Keep the documented guarantee scoped to synchronous stores; do not claim atomic rollback for Postgres.
gaps.acceptanceTest: Postgres tests document flush behavior; no false atomicity claim.

gaps.consequence: Whole-snapshot rollback can erase a concurrent lifecycle transition in the same plugin instance.
gaps.evidence: persistLifecycleChange imports the full pre-call snapshot on failure.
gaps.rootCause: No per-mission mutex; storage writes are serialized but state mutation is not.
gaps.remediation: Add per-mission lifecycle serialization or narrow the rollback; document if not fully solved.
gaps.acceptanceTest: Concurrent lifecycle failure test does not erase an unrelated mission transition.

gaps.consequence: Task records are not separately persisted; resumption needs the caller to supply the plan and relies on mission evidence.
gaps.evidence: Store has no task methods; Mission has no task ledger.
gaps.remediation: Implement resumption from mission evidence and disclose that the task plan is caller-supplied.
gaps.acceptanceTest: Resuming an active mission skips tasks whose required gates already have executed evidence.

gaps.consequence: The running plugin is stale; governance tools in this session call an older core API.
gaps.evidence: bos_start_mission failed with bos.transitionMission is not a function.
gaps.rootCause: Long-lived host loaded the plugin before the current build; no hot reload.
gaps.remediation: Restart the OpenCode host/plugin for runtime equivalence. Local MCP smoke and tests start fresh processes.
gaps.acceptanceTest: After restart, bos_start_mission succeeds against the same source.
